$comment: MACHINE-READABLE ATTRIBUTE DELTA for the FlowX onboarding spec, v1.7.1 -> v1.7.2. Intended to be fed directly to an automated agent updating the Databricks App (databricks-app/) or any other spec-authoring surface. Every path below is expressed as it appears in an onboarding spec document, rooted at the spec object; `[]` denotes an array element. NO ATTRIBUTE IS ADDED, MODIFIED OR REMOVED in this release. What changes is enforcement: previously an unrecognised attribute was accepted and silently never read; it is now a hard validation error. Any surface that emits an attribute not in the allowlists below will now fail onboarding. The enforcing artefacts are onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec.schema.json (structure; additionalProperties:false on every authored container) and spec_validator.py::reject_unknown_keys (semantics, messages quoted verbatim below).

summary.migration_required_for: Any spec (or any UI/template/generator that emits one) carrying an attribute the framework does not read. Previously accepted and ignored; now rejected at onboarding with a message naming the correct attribute. 56 of the 57 specs shipped in this repo were already clean; the one exception carried two inert root keys (environment, catalog_name) which have been deleted.

enforcement_change.title: Unknown attributes are rejected, never silently ignored
enforcement_change.rationale: A key the framework does not read still onboards, still writes its control-table row and still runs the pipeline -- while doing nothing. `data_quality` instead of `dq_config` means data quality never runs, with no signal anywhere. This is the failure mode REMOVED_*_KEYS already prevented for deleted attributes; it now covers attributes that were never real, which is overwhelmingly what a generated spec produces.
enforcement_change.trigger: presence, not truthiness -- {"infer_schema": false} is rejected exactly like {"infer_schema": true}
exemptions: any key matching ^_ (author comment; JSON has no comment syntax)
enforcement_change.message_template: <json_path>: not a recognised attribute -- the framework never reads it, so leaving it in place silently does nothing.<hint>
hint_forms: ' Use <replacement>.' when the key is in UNKNOWN_KEY_ALIASES
' Did you mean <x>?' when difflib finds a close match at cutoff 0.6

ui_actions.action: Verify every emitted attribute name appears in the matching allowlist above. Verified clean at v1.7.1: the non-matching identifiers in these files are UI section ids (src_auto, shared.target, gov, ...), not spec attributes.
Surface the rejection message verbatim. It already names the correct attribute, so echoing it is more useful than a generic 'invalid spec' error.
Call onboarding.agent_tools.validate_json (offline, no Spark) after generating and before returning; loop on errors. Golden examples to seed from: agent_skills/reference/golden_specs.json.

validation.note: validate_spec(None, spec) is supported for every flow type as of v1.7.1. The EXPLAIN-based transformation_sql/transform_sql structural check is skipped without a SparkSession (parameter substitution is still checked); it runs at onboarding time on the cluster.
